cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because this one's a big one. Some time later, God tests our friend Abraham and calls out his name. "Here I am," Abraham answers.

cards.question: God tells Abraham to take his son, his only son Isaac, whom he loves, and go to the land of ___.

cards.text: And there, on one of the mountains, God tells him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering. Yeah, you read that right, friend.

cards.question: God tells Abraham to make the offering on one of the mountains. True or false: God says He will show Abraham which one.

cards.text: So Abraham gets up early the next morning and saddles his donkey. Friend, I have hit snooze on my own OVEN TIMER, and this man is just UP.

cards.question: Abraham takes along two of his servants and his son Isaac. What else does Abraham do before he sets out?

answers.text: He splits the wood for the offering
He gathers stones for the altar
He packs gifts for the long trip

cards.question: Abraham's group heads out for the place God had designated. On the ___ day, Abraham looks up and sees it in the distance.

cards.text: Three days on the road, and I get winded walking from the oven to the cookie boxes. "Stay here with the donkey," Abraham tells his servants.

cards.question: True or false: Abraham tells his servants that he and the boy will go over there to worship, and then come back to them.
Now it's just father and son. Abraham places the ___ for the burnt offering on Isaac, and he carries the fire and the sacrificial ___ himself.

cards.text: The two of them walk on together, until Isaac speaks up: "My father!" "Here I am, my son," Abraham replies.

cards.question: Isaac looks around. The fire is here, and the wood is here. What does Isaac ask his father about?

answers.text: Where the lamb for the offering is
How much farther they have to walk

cards.question: Isaac's question about the lamb hangs in the air. What does Abraham tell his son?

answers.text: God Himself will provide the lamb
The servants will bring one up
We'll find one at the top

cards.text: And then, that line again: the two of them walk on together. I bet every step feels heavier now.
They arrive at the place God had designated. Abraham builds the altar there and arranges the wood.

cards.question: Then Abraham binds his son Isaac. Where does Abraham place him?

answers.text: On the altar atop the wood
Beside the altar on the ground
Under a tree near the altar

cards.text: Then Abraham reaches out his hand and takes the knife to slaughter his son. Friend, I am NOT breathing over here.
JUST THEN, the angel of the LORD calls out to Abraham from heaven: "Abraham, Abraham!"

cards.question: When the angel of the LORD calls, Abraham answers with the exact same words he gave God at the very start of this story. True or false?
Abraham has the knife in his hand and Isaac is on the altar. What does the angel of the LORD tell him?

answers.text: Do not lay a hand on the boy
Take the boy home with you

cards.question: The angel tells Abraham that now he knows Abraham ___ God.

cards.text: The proof is that Abraham has not withheld his only son. Okay, everybody exhale, because my mustache has been clenched this WHOLE time.
Then Abraham looks up and sees something in a thicket behind him.

cards.question: What does Abraham see in the thicket behind him?

answers.text: A ram caught by its horns
A goat tangled in the vines
A calf stuck in the brush

cards.question: Abraham takes the ram and offers it as a burnt offering in place of his ___.
Abraham gives the place on the mountain a name. What does he call it?

cards.text: And that name STICKS. So to this day it is said, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."
Then the angel of the LORD calls to Abraham from heaven a SECOND time. The LORD swears by Himself, because Abraham has done this and has not withheld his only son.

cards.question: The LORD promises to surely bless Abraham and multiply his descendants. Like what?

answers.text: The stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore
The fish in the sea and the birds in the air
The trees in the forest and the grass in the field

cards.text: And his descendants will possess the gates of their enemies. Friend, back in the junk drawer I couldn't even possess my own corner.

cards.question: The LORD keeps going with His promise. Through Abraham's offspring, who will be blessed?

answers.text: Only the people of his land

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says all nations will be blessed through Abraham's offspring because Abraham obeyed His voice.
Abraham goes back down to his servants, and they all set out together for ___.

cards.text: And Abraham settles in Beersheba. I bet that donkey was the happiest one on the trip home.

Some time later, Abraham gets news about his brother Nahor's family: Milcah has borne Nahor eight sons, and his concubine Reumah has borne four more. One name to tuck away: Nahor's son Bethuel becomes the father of Rebekah. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because Abraham's story is NOT done yet.

findings.problem: Abraham is getting up early to go and offer his son. The joke treats that as a productivity feat ('this man is just UP'), which clashes with the weight of the moment that cards 3 and 17 build. It makes light of Abraham's situation instead of fitting the tense moment.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The right answer (True) depends on both Genesis 22:1 and 22:11, since it compares Abraham's answer in each. The card cites only Genesis 22:11.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the people of his land', 'Only his own household'). That makes the right answer, 'All nations of the earth', the odd one out, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The donkey joke doesn't click. Nothing earlier sets up why the donkey would be the happiest on the trip home, so a stranger would say 'huh?'. It also lands flat right after the promise, more like a nice dad being pleasant than a real laugh.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This card is the first time Milcah shows up in the lesson, and it never says who she is. She is Nahor's wife (Genesis 11:29), with the reference.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
